t: Unless otherwise authorized by existing law, none of the funds provided in this Act, may be used by an executive branch agency to produce any prepackaged news story intended for broadcast or distribution in the United States unless the story includes a clear notification within the text or audio of the prepackaged news story that the prepackaged news story was prepared or funded by that executive branch agency.

fable.w: This is an appropriations restriction requiring executive agencies to disclose their authorship of prepackaged news stories. The tempting reading is that "notification" to the public or broadcast audiences is participation, but it is a one-way disclosure requirement, not consultation with or input from outside parties before a federal decision. No comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue is created.
fable.s: none of the funds provided in this Act, may be used by an executive branch agency to produce any prepackaged news story intended for broadcast or distribution in the United States

qwen_block.w: This section imposes a transparency requirement on federal agencies regarding the production of news stories. It does not require consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before a decision is made. The only interaction described is the inclusion of a notification in the final product, which is a disclosure rule, not a participation mechanism.
qwen_block.s: Unless otherwise authorized by existing law, none of the funds provided in this Act, may be used by an executive branch agency to produce any prepackaged news story intended for broadcast or distribution in the United States unless the story includes a clear notification within the text or audio of the prepackaged news story that the prepackaged news story was prepared or funded by that executive branch agency.

opus.w: This is a limit on how appropriated funds can be spent: agency-produced news stories must say that the agency prepared or funded them. The required 'notification' is a disclosure to the audience, not a way for outsiders to give input before a decision. No comment period, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation or right to sue is created, so the section is not participation.
opus.s: none of the funds provided in this Act, may be used by an executive branch agency to produce any prepackaged news story intended for broadcast or distribution in the United States unless the story includes a clear notification
opus.b: The tempting reading is that this involves participation because it concerns communication with the public: news stories "intended for broadcast or distribution in the United States" and a "clear notification." That reading fails. The information flows one way, from the agency out to the public. Nobody outside the government is consulted, heard from or given a role in any federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section imposes a disclosure requirement on executive branch agencies regarding prepackaged news stories. It does not require the agency to consult with the public, state governments, or other outside entities before producing the stories. The notification is a one-way communication to the audience after the content is created, which does not fit the definition of participation involving consultation or coordination before a decision.
qwen_chat.s: none of the funds provided in this Act, may be used by an executive branch agency to produce any prepackaged news story intended for broadcast or distribution in the United States unless the story includes a clear notification within the text or audio of the prepackaged news story that the prepackaged news story was prepared or funded by that executive branch agency.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that requiring a notification to the public constitutes a form of public engagement or transparency that facilitates participation. However, the definition of participation requires consultation, coordination, or interaction with outside parties *before* a decision is made, or the granting of rights to object/sue. A mandatory label on a finished product is a disclosure requirement, not a participatory process. The public is not consulted on the content, nor are they given a mechanism to influence the decision to produce the story.
